title: Saturation and tensor stability of split inclusions with contractible cokernel
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and work with small unbounded cochain complexes of $R$-modules in a fixed universe, with cochain and quasi-isomorphism conventions [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A complex $E$ is contractible if there are $R$-linear maps $h^n:E^n\to E^{n-1}$ with $d^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d^n=1_{E^n}$ for every integer $n$. Let $\mathscr S_R$ be the class of chain maps $i:X\to Y$ admitting a chain map $r:Y\to X$ with $ri=1_X$, whose cokernel complex is contractible; the cokernel has terms $Y^n/i(X^n)$ and the differential induced by $d_Y$. This class contains every isomorphism and is closed under small coproducts, pushouts along arbitrary chain maps, retracts in the arrow category, and small continuous transfinite compositions. Such a composition is a chain $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ indexed by a small ordinal, with $X_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ at each nonzero limit ordinal, in which every successor map belongs to $\mathscr S_R$; the conclusion concerns $X_0\to X_\theta$. An arrow retract means a retract through commutative squares. Every map of $\mathscr S_R$ is a chain homotopy equivalence, hence a quasi-isomorphism. Here chain homotopy equivalence means a chain map with a chain-map inverse up to homotopies of degree $-1$, with homotopy equation $f-g=dh+hd$. For every complex $K$ and $i\in\mathscr S_R$, the map $1_K\otimes_R i$ also belongs to $\mathscr S_R$, where $(K\otimes_R E)^n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}K^a\otimes_R E^b$ and $d(k\otimes e)=dk\otimes e+(-1)^a k\otimes de$ for $k\in K^a$.
